summary: Using Stark units of the z-deformation, the paper proves Taelman's class formula [Lie_E(O_L):U_St(E/O_L)]_A = L(E/O_L) for admissible Anderson A-modules over any coefficient ring A (Theorem 4.7). It shows that all Anderson F_q[t]-modules, and all A-finite or abelian Anderson modules, are admissible, and deduces the class formula for Drinfeld A-modules (Corollary 6.5). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed, and fifteen findings are recorded against HAL v2; none affects a stated result. Supplier proofs are deferred. Not formalised.

items.name: Function-field coefficient and completion datum
items.statement: Fix the coefficient datum in the conventions: A= {a in K: v_P(a)>=0 for P != infinity}, O_L is the integral closure in finite L/iota(K), and L_infinity=L tensor_K K_infinity. Infinity need not be rational, nor A principal.

api.name: FunctionFieldCoefficientData.regularAway

api.name: FunctionFieldCoefficientData.scalarTower

api.name: FunctionFieldCoefficientData.infty_degree

uses.how: Extend v_infinity to K_infinity(z) by the minimum valuation of polynomial coefficients and subtraction on quotients. Its polynomial completion is T_z(K_infinity)=F_infinity[z]((pi)); its rational completion is Ktilde_infinity=F_infinity(z)((pi)). Put Atilde=F_q(z) tensor A, Otilde_L=F_q(z) tensor O_L, and T_z(L_infinity)=L_infinity tensor_K_infinity T_z(K_infinity).

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/10: Discrete full A-lattice
uses.how: For k=F_q or F_q(z), let R=k tensor A and V a finite-dimensional k_infinity-vector space, with its valuation topology. An R-lattice M subset V is an R-submodule which is discrete and spans V over k_infinity. No freeness is part of the definition.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/20: Anderson A-module in arbitrary coefficient ring
uses.how: For a field R over F_q with iota:A->R and d>=1, an Anderson A-module is an F_q-algebra homomorphism E:A->Mat_d(R){tau}, whose constant-term map partial_E satisfies (partial_E(a)-iota(a)I)^d=0 for all a, and whose image is not contained in Mat_d(R). An integral model means every coefficient lies in O_L. Drinfeld modules are the dimension-one case.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/61: Finiteness of the affine ideal class group
uses.how: For a Dedekind k-subalgebra R of an algebraic function field F/k with fraction field F and finite k, ClassGroup(R) is finite. Apply to A, after matching its affine-model structure.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/78: Valuation bound on polynomial reciprocal roots
uses.how: Let F(z) in K_infinity[z], F(0)=1, deg F<r with r>=1, and v_infinity(F-1)>=C>=1 in the Gauss valuation. Factor F as product_(i=1)^r (1-alpha_i z), padding with zero alpha_i; then v_infinity(alpha_i)>=C/r, with v(0)=infinity.

items.name: Zeroth Fitting ideal
items.statement: For a finitely presented module M over a commutative ring R, choose R^a -> R^b -> M -> 0 and take the ideal of b by b minors; it is zero if a<b and the unit ideal for the zero module. The construction is independent of the presentation.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/6: Fitting submultiplicativity in exact sequences

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/7: Arbitrary base change of a Fitting ideal
uses.how: For a ring map f:R->S and finitely presented M, Fitt_0,S(S tensor_R M)=Ideal.map(f,Fitt_0,R(M)). In particular quotienting R by I gives the image ideal. Do not identify the image ideal with S tensor_R Fitt_0,R(M) without injectivity of its canonical map.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/8: Dedekind torsion-module elementary divisors
uses.how: For a Dedekind domain R and finitely generated torsion M, M is a finite direct sum of R/I_j for nonzero ideals I_j; Fitt_0(M)=product I_j. The ideals need not be principal.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/40: Local Fitting factor
uses.how: For a nonzero ideal I of O_L, Z_I(E/O_L)=Fitt_A(Lie_E(O_L/I)) Fitt_A(E(O_L/I))^(-1), as a fractional A-ideal inside K_infinity. Both modules are finite A-torsion modules.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/74: Residue-degree descent of the local Fitting ideal
uses.how: For finite F/F_q of degree m and any Anderson A-module E/F, there is an ideal I of A tensor_F_q F_q(z^m) such that Fitt_Atilde(Etilde(F(z)))=I Atilde. No principality is assumed here. The homogeneous-relation proof must use residue grading or Laurent localization, not the printed polynomial lower-bound condition in E10.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/13: Rank-one lattice ratio
uses.how: For one-dimensional V, choose e !=0 and write M=alpha I e, M'=alpha' I' e with nonzero fractional R-ideals I,I'. Define [M':M]_R=(alpha/alpha') I (I')^(-1) inside k_infinity. Prove independence of e and the decompositions.

uses.how: If M' subset M are R-lattices in V, M/M' is finitely generated torsion and [M:M']=Fitt_R(M/M').

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/55: Projective lift of the identity modulo z^n
uses.how: Under item 54, use the projectivity of Lie_E(O_L) over A to choose an A-linear map mu:Lie_E(O_L)->B U_z with mu(m) congruent m modulo z^n. Extend to the rational completed Lie space; its determinant lies in 1+z^n B T_z(K_infinity).

items.name: Coprime ideal factorization
items.statement: For nonzero coprime ideals I,J in O_L, Z_(IJ)=Z_I Z_J; likewise for the deformed factors. Apply the Chinese remainder isomorphism to both A-actions.

items.name: Infinitesimal layers have identical point and Lie actions
items.statement: For a nonzero ideal I and n>=1, on (I^n/I^(n+1))^d all positive Frobenius terms of E vanish since q n>=n+1. Thus E and Lie_E have the same action on this quotient, also after deformation.

items.name: Power independence of local factors
items.statement: For any nonzero ideal I and integer n>=1, Z_(I^n)=Z_I and Ztilde_(I^n)=Ztilde_I. Apply exact Fitting multiplicativity successively to the infinitesimal layers.

items.name: Radical-prime factorization
items.statement: For every nonzero I, Z_I is the product of Z_P over prime ideals P containing I, each prime once regardless of its multiplicity in I; likewise for Ztilde_I.

items.name: Integral scalar conjugation
items.statement: For xi in O_L nonzero, E'_a=xi^(-1) E_a xi has coefficients xi^(q^i-1) E_(a,i) and is integral, with partial_E'=partial_E. Its exponential is xi^(-1) exp_E xi, and xi U(E') subset U(E). The same formulas hold after z-deformation.

items.statement: Integral E satisfies (P) if there is a finite set S of nonzero primes of O_L such that for each P not in S there is x_P(z) in A[z] with Fitt_Atilde(Etilde(F_P(z)))=x_P Atilde, Fitt_A(Lie_E(F_P))=x_P(0)A, and Fitt_A(E(F_P))=x_P(1)A, where F_P=O_L/P.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/81: Uniform root bound and Euler convergence from (P')
uses.how: For a fixed separating t and E_t=sum_(i=0)^r A_i tau^i, r>=1, the norm characteristic polynomial G_P(z)/G_P(0) has degree at most d*r in Y=z^m_P, with reciprocal roots of valuation at least m_P*(-v_infinity(t))/r. Norm-factor comparison bounds the roots of x_P(z)/x_P(0) similarly, hence these ratios tend to 1 and their product is a Tate-algebra unit. The weaker unweighted Lemma 5.5 estimate also suffices for convergence with a dimension-dependent constant.

items.name: Perfect coefficient extension for motives
items.statement: Put F=L^perf and O_F the integral closure of A. Each prime P of O_L has a unique prime Q of O_F above it and O_L/P -> O_F/Q is an isomorphism. Define tau(x)=x^q and sigma(x)=x^(1/q) on F; on auxiliary z-extensions these maps fix z.

items.name: Dedekind finite-module duality
items.statement: Let k be a field, R a Dedekind k-algebra and M an R-module finite-dimensional over k. With (r.f)(m)=f(rm), Hom_k(M,k) is noncanonically isomorphic to M as an R-module. When R is a field use finite-dimensional R-linear duality; otherwise reduce to R/P^n and compare annihilator exponent and k-dimension.

uses.how: At an abelian finite-field reduction, use the skew-polynomial motive with the z-scalar convention made explicit, not the finite-dimensional point space. The tau-z presentation has cokernel the trace-adjoint action of item 95. Projectivity, the determinant-index formula and item 94 imply Fitt_Atilde(Etilde(F_P(z))) is principal. items.name: Abelian-motive cokernel and principal local ideal
items.statement: At an abelian finite-field reduction, the carrier is the motive M(E/F_P) ⊗ F_q(z) = F_P(z){τ}^d with τ twisted by z (E12). Left multiplication by τ − z is injective with cokernel F_P(z)^d carrying the trace-adjoint action of item 95 (E13, E14). Projectivity, the determinant-index formula and item 94 give Fitt_Atilde(Etilde(F_P(z))) = det(τ − z)·Atilde, principal.

items.name: Admissibility of abelian Anderson modules
items.statement: Every abelian Anderson A-module defined over O_L is admissible, using the principal local ideal at almost every reduction.

items.name: Class formula for abelian or A-finite Anderson modules
items.statement: If integral E is abelian or A-finite (either hypothesis suffices), [Lie_E(O_L):U_St]_A=L(E/O_L). Equivalently this equals [Lie_E(O_L):U]_A Fitt_A(H).

items.name: Drinfeld modules are abelian and A-finite
items.statement: Every Drinfeld A-module in the stated field setting is both abelian and A-finite; apply this to the generic fibre of an integral Drinfeld module. Proof and rank/convention dictionary are external input G6.
items.note: DM.4's motive equivalence is only over F_q[t]; the arbitrary-A proof is not supplied by that specialization. Conservatively classified as missing, pending resolution of G6.

items.name: Class formula for arbitrary-coefficient Drinfeld modules
items.statement: For any Drinfeld A-module phi defined over O_L, L(phi/O_L) is well-defined and a principal A-lattice in K_infinity, and [O_L:U_St(phi)]_A=[O_L:U(phi)]_A Fitt_A(H(phi))=L(phi/O_L). Principality is a distinct assertion requiring its local/motive justification, not a property of every Dedekind ideal.
items.note: Principality (cc-442dc5, 23 September 2026): each local factor Z_P(φ) is principal, since the reduction of φ at P is either constant (Z_P = A) or a Drinfeld module over F_P, whose Fitting ideals are generated by P_π(0) and P_π(1) for the characteristic polynomial P_π of Frobenius (Gekeler); so L(φ/O_L) is principal.

items.name: Steinitz classification of finite projectives
items.statement: For a Dedekind domain R and finite projective module P of positive rank n, there is an invertible ideal I with P isomorphic to R^(n-1) direct-sum I; the ideal class is determined by det(P). Treat rank zero separately. Apply after proving that the discrete lattices are finite torsionfree and hence projective.
items.locator: §1.3, pp. 6–7, invoking Bourbaki VII §4 no. 6; owner KTheoryLowDegrees Z.4

items.name: Ideal class group and Picard group comparison
items.statement: For a commutative domain R, there is a multiplicative equivalence ClassGroup(R) ≃ Pic(R). Transport finiteness of ClassGroup(A) through this equivalence when the source writes Pic(A).
items.locator: Lemma 5.4 and Theorem 4.7; pinned Picard-group comparison
items.note: Read Mathlib/RingTheory/PicardGroup.lean:876; only CommRing and IsDomain are required.

items.name: Norm-compatible determinant restriction of scalars
items.statement: For a finite flat extension of Dedekind domains R->S, with fraction fields K->L, restriction of two same-rank S-projective lattices identifies their relative determinant ratio with the norm of the S-relative determinant ratio. The determinant of S itself cancels only in the relative ratio. For finite S-torsion M, Fitt_R(M)=Norm_(S/R)(Fitt_S(M)).
items.locator: Theorem 4.7 proof p. 19 and Theorem 5.6 pp. 25–26; Stark units 2017 Lemma 2.10 proof; KTheoryLowDegrees Z.4
items.note: The norm/determinant transfer is explicitly in Z.4's scope. The completed-field compatibility and function-field specialization still need G4.
